jlm.en_bio: Jungian analyst, clinical social worker (MSW) and certified spiritual counselor. Certified supervisor of social work and spiritual care. Her expertise lies in the female life cycle, the mother-daughter relationship, women in the Third Age (or post menopause), divorce, loss and widowhood.
MSW in clinical Social Work, Hebrew University of Jerusalem; graduate of the 3 year program in psychoanalytic psychotherapy, the Psychological Service, Hebrew University.

MSW from The Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Graduate of the two-year 'Psychodynamic Approach when working with Adults' Program, The Academic Center for Continuing Medical Education, Tel Aviv University.
Graduate of the 'Animal Assisted Therapy' Program at the Magid Institute, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Clinical Social Worker (MSW) practicing a dynamic, integrative approach. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology from Tel Aviv University and Master’s and Doctoral degrees in Social Work from Hebrew University. Her doctoral research focused on the role and responsibility of the community in breaking the silence surrounding sexual violence and in creating alternative spaces for justice and recovery. A graduate of diverse international training programs, including Open Dialogue, SE, EMDR, and wilderness therapy, with experience treating sexual trauma and providing politically sensitive, informed therapy.

MAAT Movement Therapy, David Yellin College of Education.
Psychotherapy through conversation, embodiment, and creative methods.
Extensive experience working individually with women on personal and professional development, relationships, parenting, creative processes, and navigating crisis or trauma, depression and anxiety.
Incorporates Focusing, Family Constellations, Authentic Movement, Voice Dialogue, and STREAM (a combination of Somatic Experiencing and Movement Therapy).

MSW in clinical social work in the field of direct care, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem. BA in behavioral sciences and economics, Ben Gurion University of the Negev. Uses a dynamic approach to therapy.

Clinical Social Worker, MSW, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Specialization in feminist and gender-sensitive therapeutic approaches. Extensive experience in facilitating women’s groups.
B.A. in Sociology and Political Science and M.A. in Sociology of Education (Research Track), The Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Clinical Social Worker (MSW) with a Bachelor’s and Master’s degree in Social Work from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. Her professional experience focuses on sexuality and sexual and reproductive health, including counseling and supporting women navigating unplanned pregnancies and abortion. She is currently undertaking advanced training in sex, couples, and family therapy.

BA in Social Work and MA in Educational Counseling. Currently pursuing an MSW in Direct Practice at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Experienced in supporting individuals through crises, emotional difficulties, and trauma related challenges.

rg.en_bio: BSW, Hebrew University; MSW, Ben Gurion University; Couple & Family therapist, The Barcai Institute; Group Facilitating, Tel Aviv University.
MSW, Hebrew University; studying psychotherapy with a psychoanalytic approach, Bar Ilan University; certified Counselor in Social Work, Tel Aviv University.

PHD in Social Work, Bar Ilan University; Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy at the School of Psychotherapy TelAviv; MSW in Clinical Social Work, Bar Ilan University; B.A in Behavioural Science, Ben Gurion University.
Students supervision ,group therapy and couple therapy.
Specializing in: Crisis management, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Complex PTSD, depression and anxiety, sexual abuse, bereavement and loss, problems in couples life and parenthood.

Clinical Social Worker (MSW) , holding both a Bachelor’s and a Master’s degree in Social Work.
Graduate of the Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy Program – Winnicott Center, and certified in EMDR, Level 2.
Specializes in working with women across different life stages, addressing emotional, psychological, and existential challenges.
Integrates a psychodynamic approach with EMDR tools, tailoring each process to the unique needs of every client.

I have an MSW in clinical social work from Tel Aviv University and qualified for psychotherapy from the University of Haifa.
I am a dynamically oriented psychotherapist and have experience working in many aspects of our lives.

Social work with clinical specialization in trauma - Haifa University,
Cognitive behavioral therapy - the Israeli program for behavioral therapy
Areas of expertise:
anxiety and depression, trauma, life crises, attention deficit disorder, immigration, fertility treatments.

Clinical MSW, Children’s and Adult psychotherapy; PhD. student in the Department of Gender, Bar Ilan University, research field - motherhood. Graduated from the psychoanalytic psychotherapy program at Bar Ilan University and the children’s psychoanalytic psychotherapy program at the faculty of medicine at Tel Aviv University; MA in clinical social work from Bar Ilan University; BA in social work from Tel Aviv University. Specializing in the field of psycho-medical therapy, trauma, life crisis, depression and anxiety. Group therapist and clinical supervisor. Her private clinic is in Ramat Gan.
MSW in clinical social work, the Hebrew University, "Anthroposophic Psychotherapy, “Kelim Shluvim", Animal assisted therapy, Oranim College, BSW, the Hebrew University.
MSW in Clinical Social Work, the Hebrew University. B.A Psychology and Special Education, Tel Hai College. Certification Therapeutic Riding Instructor, TRCI.

Graduate of the Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy Program, Faculty of Medicine, Tel Aviv University.

Treats teenagers and adults and offers Parental training at a clinic in Tel Aviv.

Master of Social Work (MSW), Advanced studies in direct therapy track, Paul Baerwald School of Social Work and Social Work, Hebrew University, Jerusalem.
Specializes in gender sensitive, relational dynamic therapy. Combines multiple therapy tools (Mindfulness, Buddhism inspired treatment and trauma-informed work).

Clinical Social Worker (MSW), Tel Aviv University.
MA in Gender Studies (Bar-Ilan University) and BA in Psychology (Tel Aviv University).
Works with women facing life changes and crises, using a feminist dynamic approach.

B.A. in Behavioral Sciences, Ben-Gurion University.

In addition, I am a Trauma-Informed Yoga Teacher and provide Rehabilitation Basket (Sal Shikum) support services for individuals with Complex PTSD (CPTSD).

board.en_bio:
Joint Head, Board of Directors
A graduate of the Bet Tzvi School of Theatre Arts; BA in Law from the Chaim Shtriks Law School, the College of Administration; today she works as an attorney, specializing in the defense of human rights. Moriah was the CEO of the Counseling Center for Women from 2003 to 2011.

Joint Head, Board of Directors

Board of Directors

Assistant CEO of the Masorti Movement.

Bella is a clinical social worker and one of the founders of the Counseling Center for Women. In memory of her parents, Frieda and Arie Halpern, Bella established a fund which subsidizes psychological therapy for women of limited means. She was a pioneer in the area of awareness groups for adult children of Holocaust survivors, and published articles on the subject.

One of the founders of the Counseling Center for Women. A psychotherapist, a senior lecturer at Yeshiva University in New York and the coordinator of the Block Program for the Wurzweiler School of Social Work in Israel. Joyce has been active in feminist circles in Israel since she made aliyah more than 30 years ago: She served as the first Reform representative to be appointed to the position of member of a city religious council; she was one of the founders of the Center for Women’s Consciousness in Netanya; she is the chairperson of the ‘Gender Issues as an Area of Specialization’ committee at the Union of Social Workers in Israel. Joyce has served as a member of the Board of Directors since 2002.

has been a feminist activist since 1975 and has played a significant part in social feminist activism in Israel. She was among the founders of the Tel Aviv Rape Crisis Center, and one of the initiators of "Tz'ena Ur'ena", an organization for women's culture and feminism. In addition, she took an active part in lesbian-feminist organizations, including Aleph and Kelef. In 1990 she joined the Women's Counseling Center as a therapist, where she worked until mid-2024. Since 2025 she has served as a member of the center's Board of Directors.

Holds an LL.B. from Tel Aviv University and an M.A. in General History from The Hebrew University of Jerusalem. Ayala currently serves as Chief of Staff to the Chairman of the Board of Directors at a leading Israeli bank. With extensive legal experience specializing in labor and employment law, she previously served as the bank’s Legal Counsel for Human Resources.

mgmt.en_bio:
Ronit is a clinical social worker with a specialization in trauma. She received her MA from Haifa University.
For over a decade Ronit held several executive positions and prior to her start at CCW, she was the Director of Administration, Quality and Regulation in the Department of Mental Health in the Ministry of Health.
Ronit has extensive experience in treating sexually abused women. At the Bnei Zion Medical Center she was a therapist and group coordinator.

Clinical social worker and psychotherapist, certified supervisor in Social Work by the Tel Aviv University, lecturer.

Lecturer in the psychodynamic psychotherapy program for the treatment of sexual trauma, Bar-Ilan University.
During studies in the Relational Psychotherapy Approach, the program for advanced studies in psychotherapy,
Faculty of Medicine, Tel Aviv University.

Over the last fifteen years I have worked with women in various settings:
As a doula, shiatsu therapist for women, family constellation therapist.
I believe that working with women further connects me to that world and I feel at home.
Throughout the years I learned a great deal and I participated in various professional
trainings – massage for pregnant women, doula certification, therapist through the

Tali holds a B.A. in English Literature and an M.A. in Communication (Research Track) from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, as well as a Certified Information Specialist diploma from Beit Berl College. Over the past several years, she has worked in nonprofit organizations and healthcare institutions in information and knowledge management roles. She believes in the transformative power of feminist psychotherapy to foster personal growth and social change and sees mental health care as an essential pathway to women's well-being and empowerment.
